tour.name: Tuscany Private Day Trip from Florence: Siena, San Gimignano & Chianti Wine Tasting
tour.subtitle: A private day in the Tuscan hills with a licensed guide and car: medieval Siena and its shell-shaped Piazza del Campo, the towers of San Gimignano, and lunch with a Chianti Classico tasting at a family wine estate.
tour.seoTitle: Siena, San Gimignano & Chianti Private Day Trip | TRAVSUS
tour.metaDescription: Private Tuscany day trip from Florence: guided visit of Siena, Piazza del Campo and the cathedral, lunch and Chianti Classico tasting at a family winery, and the medieval towers of San Gimignano. Car, guide and lunch.

tour.overview:
Between Florence and Siena lie the Chianti hills, a landscape of vineyards, olive groves, stone farmhouses and rows of cypresses that has hardly changed since Renaissance painters used it as a background. The black rooster on bottles of Chianti Classico recalls the old league of villages that defended this border between two rival republics. To the south, Siena kept its Gothic centre almost untouched after its defeat by Florence in the 16th century, and to the west, San Gimignano still shows the towers its merchant families built to show off their wealth. Both towns are UNESCO World Heritage Sites, San Gimignano since 1990 and Siena since 1995.

This private day lets you enjoy Tuscany without driving or worrying about how much wine you taste. Your guide shows you Siena in the morning, its great square and its cathedral; you have lunch at a family wine estate in Chianti with a tasting of their wines and olive oil; and in the afternoon you climb the lanes of San Gimignano, with time for a famous gelato, before driving back through the hills to Florence.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Florence
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; about 5 km on sloping streets in Siena and San Gimignano

WHAT YOU SEE
• Siena: Piazza del Campo, the Palazzo Pubblico and the Torre del Mangia (outside), and the cathedral.
• A family wine estate in Chianti.
• San Gimignano: Piazza della Cisterna, Piazza del Duomo and the towers.
• The Chianti hills and their scenic roads.

WHY THIS WORKS
We reach Siena before the coaches, eat at a working estate rather than a tourist restaurant, and see San Gimignano in the late afternoon light, when the day-trippers have gone.

WHO IT SUITS
Wine lovers, couples, families and anyone who wants to see the Tuscan countryside as well as its art cities.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you prefer a shorter day with less driving, choose our Pisa and Lucca tour. If you have not yet seen Florence itself, start with our Florence tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Siena's centre is closed to cars, so you walk in from the edge of town. On 2 July and 16 August, Palio days, Siena is packed and we change the order of the day. Children receive grape juice and local snacks at the tasting.

days.name: Siena, lunch and wine tasting in Chianti, and the towers of San Gimignano
days.description:
What to expect: two medieval hill towns and the vineyards between them, with a licensed guide, private car, cathedral ticket and a winery lunch.

Your driver collects you at your Florence hotel at about 8:00 and takes the fast road south to Siena, about an hour away. Your guide leads you through the gates and down the lanes to the Piazza del Campo, the sloping, shell-shaped square divided into nine sections in memory of the Council of Nine that governed the city in its golden age. Here, twice a year on 2 July and 16 August, the city's districts race bareback horses around the square in the Palio, a tradition going back to the Middle Ages. Above it rise the Palazzo Pubblico and the slender Torre del Mangia, 102 metres tall.

You climb to the cathedral, striped in black and white marble, the colours of the city's coat of arms. Inside, the floor is covered with 56 inlaid marble panels made over two centuries, the pulpit was carved by Nicola Pisano, and the Piccolomini Library glows with frescoes by Pinturicchio. You have a little free time for a coffee or to taste ricciarelli, Siena's almond biscuits.

At about 12:30 you drive into the Chianti hills, along roads lined with cypresses, to a family wine estate. After a short walk among the vines and through the cellar, you sit down to a Tuscan lunch – crostini, pici pasta, cured meats and pecorino cheese – with a tasting of three or four wines, including their Chianti Classico, and the estate's olive oil. In the afternoon you continue to San Gimignano, the 'medieval Manhattan'. Of the more than 70 towers once built by its rival families, 14 still stand. You walk through Piazza della Cisterna and Piazza del Duomo, can taste the town's crisp white Vernaccia wine and the gelato that has won world championships, and look out from the walls over the hills. You are back at your hotel in Florence at about 18:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:00 – Pick-up at your hotel in Florence.
09:15 – Guided walk in Siena: Piazza del Campo, the cathedral.
11:45 – Free time in Siena.
12:30 – Drive into Chianti.
13:00 – Vineyard walk, lunch and wine tasting.
15:15 – Drive to San Gimignano.
15:45 – San Gimignano with your guide and free time.
17:15 – Drive back to Florence.
18:00 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• The cathedral floor is fully uncovered only for a few weeks a year, usually from late June to late July and from mid-August to mid-October.
• On Palio days and the days before, Siena is very crowded; we then visit San Gimignano first.
• Monteriggioni, a small walled village, can be added as a short stop.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Siena Cathedral ticket, lunch with wine and olive oil tasting, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Torre del Mangia and Palazzo Pubblico, gelato, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: How much driving is there?
faq.answer: About 3 hours in total, split into short stretches of 30 to 60 minutes through beautiful countryside.

faq.question: How much wine is served?
faq.answer: Usually three or four wines in tasting portions with lunch. You never have to drive, and non-alcoholic drinks are always available.

faq.question: Can children join the wine tasting?
faq.answer: Children are very welcome. They receive grape juice or soft drinks and the same lunch; the vineyard walk is popular with them.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes, the ticket to Siena Cathedral. The Torre del Mangia, the Palazzo Pubblico and San Gimignano's towers can be added.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a Tuscan lunch at the wine estate. Vegetarian, gluten-free and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: Is there much walking?
faq.answer: About 5 km on sloping streets and some steps. Siena's centre is closed to cars, so you walk in from the edge of town.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. Both towns are on hills with steep lanes. The car can get closer in San Gimignano, and the winery is easy. Tell us your needs and we will adapt.

faq.question: Can we buy wine at the estate?
faq.answer: Yes, if you wish, with no obligation. Most estates can ship wine to your home country.

faq.question: Can we visit Pisa on the same day?
faq.answer: It makes the day too long to enjoy. We suggest our separate Pisa and Lucca tour, or replacing San Gimignano with Pisa in a custom version.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes and, for the cathedral, clothes covering shoulders and knees. A layer for the cool cellar.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: Every season has its charm: spring flowers, summer sun, the grape harvest in September and October, and quiet winter days. Avoid Siena on Palio days unless you want to see the race.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
